## Possible Titles

- Agents, Responsibility, and the Cost of Going Faster
- The Irony of 10x
- More Output, Less Upside
- When AI Made Me Faster and Poorer
- Being Crushed by Responsibility

## Working Angle

This should probably be a personal essay, not a manifesto about AI. The core tension:

- agents made me dramatically more productive
- that productivity increased the responsibility I carry
- the financial upside I used to realize personally has gone down, not up

## Section Stub: Opening Scene

Prompt:

- Start with a concrete moment. Maybe reviewing a massive PR from the intern / contractor side of the system.
- What did I feel in that moment: confusion, dread, pressure, responsibility, skepticism?
- What was the specific thought: "I might own all of this later, even if I did not really produce or validate all of it myself."
- Can I open with one sharp sentence that names the tension right away?

Possible opener idea:

"Agentic coding has made me faster than ever, but it has also made me feel responsible for more than I can honestly hold in my head."

## Section Stub: This Is About Me, Not Everyone

Prompt:

- Add a strong caveat early: this is not prediction, prescription, or universal truth.
- Name my context: big company, internal platform work, political environment, mixed team ownership, frontier models via Copilot.
- What about my temperament matters here? Hyperfocus, initiative, problem solving, pressure sensitivity, desire to meet expectations.
- What would I want a reader to not mishear?

## Section Stub: Who I Was Before Agents

Prompt:

- Briefly describe my work history and self-understanding.
- I am not formally trained, so what made me valuable anyway?
- What does it mean that people were impressed before AI too?
- Pull in relevant threads from `pages/blog/forge-ahead.md`: prior projects, practical problem solving, being useful, learning systems by doing.
- What gifts do I think God gave me that made me effective before this shift?

Questions to answer:

- What kind of worker was I before agents entered my workflow?
- What did I already know how to do well?
- What part of my value came from focus rather than brilliance?

## Section Stub: Why I Leaned Into Agentic Coding

Prompt:

- Explain that I did not stumble into this accidentally; I chose to go hard.
- Why did it feel natural to me to adopt agents aggressively?
- What about the mission at Caterpillar Autonomy made the leap feel worth it?
- Pull in `pages/blog/cat-autonomy-2-0.md`: I stayed because the work felt meaningful, not merely because it was interesting.
- Mention harness engineering / Nexus / experimentation if it helps show this was a deliberate investment.

Questions to answer:

- Why did I trust this direction enough to reorganize my work around it?
- Was I chasing novelty, usefulness, recognition, mission, or all of the above?

## Section Stub: What Actually Changed

Prompt:

- Describe the practical change in my day-to-day work.
- I am no longer mainly writing code line by line; I am directing, reviewing, testing, and integrating generated work.
- What changed about the quantity of output?
- What changed about how coworkers and managers perceived me?
- What changed about the kind of questions people started asking me?

Questions to answer:

- When did I realize this was not just autocomplete, but a new mode of working?
- What does "enterprise-grade work fully written and produced by agents" actually mean in practice?

## Section Stub: The Hidden Cost of Speed

Prompt:

- Write about the gap between output and understanding.
- I can ship more, but I do not always know the code as intimately as hand-written systems I built before.
- Testing is not the same as ownership.
- Documentation existing is not the same as confidence.
- What kinds of future problems does speed create?

Questions to answer:

- What do I know I have not fully read?
- What kinds of bugs or maintenance traps am I afraid I am creating?
- What does it feel like to build something that works but still feels partially foreign?

## Section Stub: Responsibility Without Clear Boundaries

Prompt:

- This may be the emotional center before the money section.
- Describe the contractor / intern dynamic and why it intensifies the burden.
- Their output can become my long-term maintenance problem.
- The organization sees me as someone who understands AI and agents, so responsibility pools onto me.
- Ask whether the pressure is explicit or self-imposed, but note that the body feels it either way.

Questions to answer:

- Who is actually accountable when AI-assisted code breaks six months from now?
- What does it mean to be treated like the local expert when I do not feel like one?
- Why is being noticed beginning to feel costly instead of rewarding?

## Section Stub: The Financial Irony

Prompt:

- State this clearly and concretely.
- For years, I realized more value from my output because I worked two jobs concurrently.
- Due to the new role, new responsibility, and the demands of agentic coding in this environment, I had to go down to one job.
- So the irony is: the tools make me dramatically more productive, but I personally realize less economic upside from my own gifts and skills than I did before.
- Keep this grounded and honest, not whiny.

Questions to answer:

- What exactly have I lost financially?
- Why does this feel bigger than "I want more money"?
- Where do the gains of AI go when an individual contributor gets faster?
- If I can now produce 10x more code, why does my life not feel lighter, freer, or better compensated?

Possible thesis sentence:

"Agentic coding increased the value I create at work, while decreasing the share of that value I personally get to realize."

## Section Stub: Mission, Meaning, and Fatigue

Prompt:

- Reaffirm the good: this is meaningful work, and that matters to me.
- Tie back to autonomy, safety, and the reasons I stayed at Caterpillar.
- Then tell the truth: meaning does not cancel fatigue.
- What has already started to feel tired, dulled, or overdrawn in me?

Questions to answer:

- What purpose did this role awaken in me?
- Why does that sense of purpose already feel threatened?
- How do I talk honestly about fatigue without pretending I am fully burned out if I am not sure?

## Section Stub: Questions I Cannot Yet Answer

Prompt:

- Let the essay breathe here instead of forcing a neat conclusion.
- Gather the real unresolved questions.
- If I stopped using agents, would I still impress people?
- Would I solve fewer problems or create fewer future ones?
- Am I carrying real expectations or anticipated ones?
- Is this making me a better engineer, or just a faster source of output and responsibility?

## Section Stub: Conclusion

Prompt:

- End modestly, not with a manifesto.
- I am not anti-AI.
- I am not saying agents are bad.
- I am trying to tell the truth about what this transition has cost me personally.
- Land on the mismatch between speed, responsibility, and reward.

Possible closing direction:

- The tools are real.
- The gains are real.
- The responsibility is real.
- The redistribution of value is also real.
- I am still trying to understand what faithfulness looks like inside that tension.

## Material To Weave In

- My lack of formal software engineering background
- My history of being useful by solving practical problems quickly
- My tendency toward hyperfocus and over-responsibility
- The shift from hand-written confidence to agent-mediated uncertainty
- The contractor / intern maintenance concern
- The drop from two incomes to one
- The irony that Cat benefits more from my increased output than I do
- The Christian framing around calling, providence, stewardship, and fatigue

## Things To Avoid

- sounding like I am making universal claims about all AI use
- sounding bitter without being specific
- centering line-count metrics too much without translating them into responsibility
- pretending I have fully landed on a conclusion
- making this a complaint post about coworkers instead of a reflection on burden and change

items.title: I Was Saved From A Cult
items.content_html:
Introduction #

I’m getting coffee with a guy from church today, we’re planning to swap some stories about how the Lord has worked in our lives in a few specific ways. He has some history in the New Age movement, and I’m very interested in that story. My offering to him will be my own story, fairly short it might be, of how God protected me from long-term involvement in a hypercharasmatic cult.

Theological Context #

This dove-tails well with Andrew’s sermon yesterday, noting that in many Charasmatic circles the gift of the Holy Spirit becomes more important than the person of Jesus who gives the Spirit, and who gives Salvation. This is the crux of my own experience as well.

The Group #

The group was called “Wind and Fire Ministries” and they had their own purpose-built building out in the middle of nowhere, but close enough for me to drive to. I grew up in Iowa, a 10 minute drive on the interstate landed you pretty quick in the scene of any low-budget horror movie. The building was definitely nice, there was even some land, but there was nothing around it.

How I Got Involved #

I barely remember how I got involved - a kid I was in high school with went there regularly and then one adult who helped out in my church’s youth group did as well. I can still vividly remember him telling me about an experience he had at this place - a “slayed in the spirit” kind of experience.

My Experience #

I was hungry, desperate even, for spiritual experiences and this “ministry” was extremely welcoming and accessible. My parents didn’t know anything about what went on there, and to be fair they didn’t do a ton of ultra-weird stuff when I was there… flag-waving and tongues were enough to probably ruffle some fundie feathers. I never fell to the ground shaking or spoke in tongues (not for lack of awkwardly trying upon the instruction of a member there though). I remember going one night and staying for hours while the head honcho was doing annointings with oil and I wanted to be annointed because I wanted to speak in tongues because I wanted an “experience”. By God’s grace I was never given a super emotional experience there - the emphasis was always on gifts and supernatural things, not on the person and work of the Lord Jesus

Expectations, Intimacy, and Shared Life

Purpose #

To surface unspoken expectations and ground shared life; emotionally, spiritually, and physically, in service to the Lord and each other.

Key Scriptures #

1 Corinthians 7:1–5; Hebrews 13:4; Proverbs 24:3–4; Ecclesiastes 4:9–12

1 Corinthians 7:1–5 (LEB)

7Now concerning the things about which you wrote: “It is good for a man not to touch a woman.” 2 But because of sexual immorality, let each man have his own wife and let each woman have her own husband. 3 The husband must fulfill his obligation to his wife, and likewise also the wife to her husband. 4 The wife does not have authority over her own body, but her husband does. And likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but his wife does. 5 Do not defraud one another, except perhaps by agreement, for a time, in order that you may devote yourselves to prayer, and then you should be together again, lest Satan tempt you because of your lack of self control.

Hebrews 13:4

Marriage must be held in honor by all, and the marriage bed be undefiled, because God will judge sexually immoral people and adulterers.

Proverbs 24:3-4

3 By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established. 4 And by knowledge, rooms are filled with all riches, precious and pleasant.

Ecclesiastes 4:9-12

9 Two are better than the one, for they enjoy a better reward for their toil. 10 For if they fall, one will help up his companion. But pity the one who falls and there is no one to help him up. 11 Also if two lie together, they can keep each other warm. But how can one person be warm? 12 Although an assailant may overpower one person, two may withstand him. A threefold cord is not easily broken!

Themes #

Many marital wounds come from unspoken expectations.

  • Not just unspoken, but a pattern of letting your expectations be unmet can lead to strife.
  • It’s up to both people in the marriage to be on the lookout: remember, together you face unspoken expectations, you do not face each other’s expectations, be united

Intimacy is covenantal and requires safety, communication, and grace.

  • No one is safer to talk to than your spouse (within reason, I think there’s a place for men’s/women’s group kind of stuff, pastoral counseling, etc. but in general no one should be safer to share something with than your spouse)

Faithfulness is sustained through shared rhythms and priorities.

  • Patterns are powerful
  • In our lives, I for sure notice when we slip into patterns of lack-of-intimacy or communication, and the longer you “get by” the easier it is to live that way
  • “Missing something once is a mistake, missing something twice is the start of a new habit.” The point being that it takes work to communicate, and you should plan to communicate often. Missing a date, or an agreed-upon-time to talk about something once is just a mistake, but don’t let yourselves push off hard conversations (either together or individually)

Discussion Prompts #

Expectations #

What are you most looking forward to in daily married life?

What concerns you about sharing life so closely?

Intimacy #

How do you communicate needs, boundaries, and fears?

  • with great trust in your spouse
  • openly, hopefully.
  • do not assume the first thing said is what is meant, maybe you need to work through it together to figure out what one of you needs

How will you protect intimacy after marriage?

Shared Life #

How do you approach money and financial decisions?

  • Our approach: God gives us everything and we recognize that any ordered system requires a hierarchy of decision makers. I “make the final decision” which is often to trust what Kassia wants to do with some money. Kassia asks me about financial things, not for permission, but for information. Then from the information, we decide together and if we disagree it’s up to me to put my foot down on it or defer to her in our disagreement (both circumstances happen)

What rhythms help you remain spiritually grounded?

Mentor Contribution #

Share principles, not details, regarding intimacy and finances.

Emphasize patience, mutual service, and long-term faithfulness.

Communication, Conflict, and Forgiveness

Purpose #

To normalize conflict and equip the couple to handle it with humility, clarity, and grace.

Key Scriptures #

James 1:19–20; Proverbs 15:1; Ephesians 4:25–32; Matthew 18:21–35

James 1:19–20 (LEB): 19 Understand this, my dear brothers: every person must be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger, 20 for human anger does not accomplish the righteousness of God.

Proverbs 15:1 (LEB): A soft answer will turn away wrath, but a word of trouble will stir anger.

Ephesians 4:25–32 (LEB): 25 Therefore, putting aside the lie, speak truth each one of you with his neighbor, because we are members of one another. 26 Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun set on your anger, 27 nor give place to the devil. 28 The one who steals must steal no longer, but instead must labor, working with his own hands what is good, so that he may have something to share with the one who has need. 29 No rotten word must proceed from your mouth, but only something good for the building up of the need, in order that it may give grace to those who hear, 30 and do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. 31 All bitterness, and rage, and wrath, and clamor, and abusive speech, must be removed from you, together with all wickedness. 32 Become kind toward one another, compassionate, forgiving one another, just as also God in Christ has forgiven you.

Matthew 18:21–35 (LEB): 21 Then Peter came up to him and said, “Lord, how many times will my brother sin against me and I will forgive him? Up to seven times?” 22 Jesus said to him, “I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven! 23 “For this reason the kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man—a king—who wanted to settle accounts with his slaves. 24 And when he began to settle them, someone was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents. 25 And because he did not have enough to repay it, the master ordered him to be sold, and his wife and his children and everything that he had, and to be repaid. 26 Then the slave threw himself to the ground and began to do obeisance to him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will pay back everything to you!’ 27 So the master of that slave, because he had compassion, released him and forgave him the loan. 28 But that slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii, and taking hold of him, he began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back everything that you owe!’ 29 Then his fellow slave threw himself to the ground and began to implore him, saying, ‘Be patient with me and I will repay you!’ 30 But he did not want to, but rather he went and threw him into prison until he would repay what was owed. 31 So when his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were extremely distressed, and went and reported to their master everything that had happened. 32 Then his master summoned him and said to him, ‘Wicked slave! I forgave you all that debt because you implored me! 33 Should you not also have shown mercy to your fellow slave as I also showed mercy to you?’ 34 And because he was angry, his master handed him over to the merciless jailers until he would repay everything that was owed. 35 So also my heavenly Father will do to you, unless each of you forgives his brother from your hearts!”

Themes #

Conflict reveals the heart; it does not create sin.

Patterns of hostility matter more than isolated arguments.

  • But do not allow yourself to over-generalize in your frustration: “He always …”, “She never …”
  • I probably struggled with this in reading far too much into arguments and taking Kassia’s frustration with me way too personally, creating hostility when there was only frustration

True repentance and forgiveness are essential marital practices.

  • Your stuck with your person, are you going to stay frustrated forever?
  • Remind yourself of the gospel at every argument, “Jesus has forgiven me so much more than I am/feel owed by my spouse right now”

Discussion Prompts #

What is your instinct under tension: withdrawal, pursuit, defensiveness?

What makes it hard for you to apologize or forgive?

  • For me it is correctness: I find it hard to apologize for trying to be correct (or understood) when that pursuit ends up hurting Kassia in some way

Covenant, Calling, and Friendship

Purpose #

To establish a biblical vision of marriage that shapes expectations, priorities, and endurance.

Key Scriptures #

Genesis 2:18–25; Malachi 2:14; Ephesians 5:31–32; Proverbs 18:22

Genesis 2:18-25

18 Then the Lord God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper (עֵ֫זֶר |e-zer ) corresponding (נֶ֫גֶד | ne-ged) to him.” 19 The Lord God formed out of the ground every wild animal and every bird of the sky, and brought each to the man to see what he would call it. And whatever the man called a living creature, that was its name. 20 The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the sky, and to every wild animal; but for the man no helper was found corresponding to him. 21 So the Lord God caused a deep sleep to come over the man, and he slept. God took one of his ribs and closed the flesh at that place. 22 Then the Lord God made the rib he had taken from the man into a woman and brought her to the man. 23 And the man said: This one, at last, is bone of my bone and flesh of my flesh; this one will be called “woman,” for she was taken from man. 24 This is why a man leaves his father and mother and bonds with his wife, and they become one flesh. 25 Both the man and his wife were naked, yet felt no shame.

helper corresponding

This is the helper opposite him - balance

Malachi 2:14

And you ask, “Why?” Because even though the Lord has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, you have acted treacherously against her. She was your marriage partner and your wife by covenant.

God as the witness

“the wife of your youth” Since a Jewish marriage was religious and involved a covenant, God served as the witness (Mal 2:10). Thus, a Jewish man abandoning his Jewish wife was tantamount to abandoning a vow to God Himself.

Ephesians 5:31-32

31 For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh. 32 This mystery is profound, but I am talking about Christ and the church.

Proverbs 18:22

A man who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the Lord.

Themes #

Marriage is covenantal, not consumerism sustained by feelings.

  • Serving your spouse is serving the Lord, as long as you both seek to serve Jesus then you will naturally (since it’s a natural consequence of serving the Lord) serve one another with the right heart. Your service is not to each other directly, it is to the Lord

God uses marriage as a primary means of sanctification.

  • Parenting is hard because you are forced to put your needs on hold for the sake of your kids sometimes, but love makes it easier and kids are level 2. Level 1 is your spouse - as you put your needs on hold for your spouse Jesus changes your heart to help you really see that other person as equally as valuable as yourself. Not necessarily more valuable, that isn’t the point, the point is that the ground is level at the foot of the cross, and daily consistent rendering of service to your spouse as to the Lord is a transformative experience in the direction of seeing others how Jesus does.

Friendship and unity go right along with roles, logistics, and preferences.

  • Dedicate yourselves to the Lord and friendship will follow.

Discussion Prompts #

What do you believe makes a marriage “successful”?

  • calm and charitable disagreement
  • established and respected order
    • Devin will be the head
    • the head of the body should probably listen to the body quite intensely before making decisions…
  • do people outside your marriage see Jesus as a crucial player in your relationship or is all about the 2 of you? Culture would have it look like 2 puzzle pieces that fit together perfectly, but the reality is that a godly marriage should frame the gospel. When people look at your relationship, they shouldn’t just see 2 best friends in love, they should somewhat immediately see and know about Jesus’ role in your relationship

Where do you think cultural ideas about marriage fall short?

  • literally everywhere

What promises feel most weighty to you as you think about your vows?

How do you currently cultivate friendship and closeness?

Mentor Contribution #

Share briefly how covenant faithfulness has shaped your own marriage.

Share how unity is built intentionally over time, not assumed.

Reflection #

What do you hope God will form in you through marriage?

Premarital Session 2 - March 2026 Premarital Session 3 April 2026

Note: this began in Event Details Updates via Notifications as a Service and is the first iteration of this idea

Projects #

  • Soonish
  • Mindful

Docs #

  • Consider the Pushover Docs for inspiration on notifiq docs as well

Notes #

Use Cases #

  • Event Details and updates
  • IT ticketing system
  • Volunteer reminder system

Requirements #

  1. apprise server/library
  2. CMS with users and roles + a database
  • updates need to POST to apprise
  1. notification backbone
  • SMS
  • email (requires domain to offer a real service)
    • maybe managers could bring their own email server?
    • no, just make it configurable - people setup the whole thing or they pay me
  1. infra
  • Temporal instead of webserver patterns may lead to easier scaling

Drafting #

  • Been working in Windsurf with gpt-5 mostly on outlining the requirements for soonish
  • My immediate goal is to have very detailed specs for the project to best utilize AI while building it without allowing the AI to drive any meaningful aspect of the development

Ideas #

  • WorkOS for auth for B2B for soonish
  • remind.notifiq.net/ as a usecase for soonish
    • configured reading times, so just get reminded at the next one
    • phase 2 of this idea might be grabbing the content of the url and sending the notification with some of that content

Message Priority #

  • Events should have a priority of some kind so that business hours can be considered easily
  • Should channels have similar types of preferences? I suppose I need to think about the different user flows
    • automated event makes critical ticket outside business hours - force update subscribers based on…. whatever they’re subscribed with/desired channels
    • event update is critical - all subscribers need to know on their desired channels
    • those above 2 are the same
    • event update is not critical - do the signal to everyone but channels take into consideration that it’s info only, so respect a business hours/quiet hours and notify during appropriate time.

Frontends #

  • Use NiceGUI for a default events front end as a toy example to demonstrate notifiq use cases

  • Use react for something like pager duty maybe - just to see what kind of things windsurf can do with it

Competitors #

  • zenduty

Progress #

November 22 2025 #

  • added auto-sub of creator to event (visibility)
    • auto subscription_selector made for autosub:default
    • subscription_selector for event.tag == channel.tag as well

items.content_html:
Work Compensation Notes #

  • Anthony asked me what I needed to be happy and I didn’t have a good answer, but I did ask for clarity on the chaos at work. I’ve thought more about it and I think I’ll just be honest with him. I have moon-lit in the past, exceeded expectations at Cat, and made double my salary. I don’t need to go back to that, but I want to ask him what he makes in total comp and what the horizon looks like for me at Cat. Not because I want prestige, but because I want to prioritize my family and if I can give financial freedom to them (and myself) much earlier than if I was solo-loyal to Cat, that’s a real thing I need to wrestle with. So my question for him will be how much of that gap can Cat close over time?
